description: Check EVERY number in one of your own reports against the filing it cites, in one call. Returns a verdict per figure: `matches` (the prose quotes the filing's own rendered string), `differs` (positive evidence the filing says something else — the report is wrong), or `not_checkable` (no comparison was possible). CALL THIS BEFORE `publish_report` OR `sign_off_report`. `publish_report` REFUSES a report carrying an unreviewed `differs`, so running this first is how you find out what to fix instead of being refused. TO FIX A `differs`: rewrite the figure by quoting `verdict.display` character-for-character (or `verdict.derived_quarterly_display` if you meant the quarter rather than the year-to-date number) with `update_report`, then call this again. A non-empty `verdict.scope` means the citation points at the WRONG FILING — re-quoting will not fix that; correct the citation. If the report's number is right and the comparison is not (an external source, a deliberate restatement), record a human disposition with `save_figure_review` — a reviewed figure no longer blocks publishing. ⚠️ `not_checkable` IS NOT A PASS AND IS NOT A RETRY. It means nobody compared anything — a figure with no fact, a fact with no rendered string, a lookup that failed. Report it as unverified; do not call the tool again expecting a different answer, and never present it as verified. Expect it to be a large share of any real report. `untraced` is counted separately from `not_checkable` on purpose: a figure that never had a source is a different finding from one whose source could not be read. Nothing here is stored — a verdict is recomputed every call, because a later filing can restate a number and an edit changes a figure's identity. Only the report's author can verify it; a report that is not yours is indistinguishable from one that does not exist. Tier: sp500+ (sample rejected). Free — provenance calls are never charged.

report_id.description: Identifier of the report to verify, as returned by create_report / list_my_reports / save_freeform_report. Must be authored by the calling customer.

name: verify_report_figures

_meta.description: Provenance envelope — data lineage for every MCP response

cost_usd.description: Per-call cost transparency. Omitted for subscription-only tools that have no PAYG-equivalent price.

basis.description: payg_charge = real agent-pay charge. payg_rate_card = indicative price, not billed.

billed.description: true = this amount was actually charged via PAYG for this call. false = indicative PAYG-equivalent value; your plan already covers this call for free.

data_plan.description: Access plan: sample | sp500 | pro | full

data_quality.description: Server-side invariants run on this response

fundamentals_as_of.description: ISO timestamp when the FINANCIAL STATEMENTS were last rebuilt in bulk. Use THIS — not `last_updated` — when telling a user how current the cross-sectional fundamentals are. The snapshot is republished on every weekday price refresh while the statements are carried forward unchanged, so `last_updated` can be far more recent than the numbers it sits next to. It is a floor for a single filer, not a ceiling: a filer with a live partition receives its filing, facts and ratios intraday (minutes after EDGAR dissemination), so an entity-scoped read may carry a filing newer than this; cross-sectional ranks (factor scores, earnings signals) refresh with the weekly bulk export.

last_updated.description: ISO timestamp when the snapshot was exported

latency_ms.description: Wall-clock milliseconds this tool call took, measured server-side around the handler.

limit_warnings.description: Soft-warning array for partial fulfillment. Each entry carries a stable subcode + remediation.options[]. AI agents pattern-match on subcode.

payg_override.description: Set when this single response was paid for via the agent-pay PAYG flow — the rate-limit / depth-limit checks were bypassed for this call only.

pit_safe.description: true iff a zero-look-ahead point-in-time cut was applied to every returned figure

price_as_of.description: ISO timestamp when the price surfaces were last refreshed.

reset_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the window resets

truncation.description: Set when fewer rows were returned than requested — explains why and points to a remedy

byState.description: Human review marks by state: verified, corrected, external, rejected.

differs.description: Traced, unreviewed, and the filing contradicts the quote — a SUBSET of `unresolved`.

reviewed.description: Figures carrying a human review mark, whatever its state.

traced.description: Figures that resolved to a fact_id.

unresolved.description: Outstanding: no evidence of any kind, OR traced to a fact whose filing says something else. These are what a human is shown and what blocks sign-off.

figures.description: One entry per distinct figure in the report's prose. An empty array means the report states no numbers.

fact_id.description: The fact this figure resolved to; null when nothing traced it.

figure_key.description: Stable identity of this figure — the exact key `save_figure_review` is written against.

raw.description: The token exactly as the prose writes it. Never reformatted.

reviewed.description: Does a human review mark already exist for this key? A mark ends the question — including for a `differs`.

section_id.description: The report section the figure appears in.

against.description: Which rendered string the prose matched: `display` (the filing's own figure) or `derived_quarterly_display` (the three-month figure derived from a year-to-date filing).

derived_quarterly_display.description: The derived three-month figure, rendered. If the report meant the QUARTER rather than the year-to-date number, this is the string to quote instead.

display.description: What the filing says, already rendered. QUOTE THIS character-for-character to fix the report.

figure.description: The figure EXACTLY as the report writes it — the string that is wrong.

scope.description: Declared filing fields the lineage CONTRADICTS — `ticker`, `form_type`, `period_end`. Empty when only the value differs. A non-empty scope means the citation points at the wrong filing, so re-quoting `display` will not fix it.

reason.description: Why no comparison happened: `no_fact` (the figure was never traced to a fact), `no_display` (the fact carries no rendered string), `fact_not_found`, `lineage_unreadable`, `lookup_failed`, `rate_limited`. ⚠️ NOT A PASS — this figure needs a human, not a retry.

additionalProperties.description: Full provenance for one fact. Identity: fact_id, entity_id, ticker, company_name, concept, standard_concept, accession_id. Value: numeric_value (raw), `display` (the SAME number already rendered — "$391.04B" — QUOTE THIS rather than re-rounding numeric_value yourself), unit, plus derived_quarterly_value/derived_quarterly_display (a Q2/Q3 10-Q states year-to-date, so the quarter and the filing are different numbers). Filing: source_url, inline_viewer_url, document_url, filing_date, form_type, accepted_at. Duration: period_start, period_end, period_span_days, and period_type (instant | quarterly | half_year | nine_month | annual | duration) so a 3-month stub is never mistaken for the 12-month figure — a 10-K tags BOTH at the same period_end. ⚠️ There is no `value` key and no `cik` key; the fields are named exactly as emitted.

accepted_at.description: SEC acceptance timestamp (ISO 8601) — the moment this number became public. The PIT cut is taken on this.

accession_id.description: SEC accession number of the filing that reported this value, e.g. 0000320193-24-000123.

concept.description: Raw XBRL tag as the filer used it, e.g. us-gaap:Revenues.

derived_quarterly_display.description: `derived_quarterly_value` rendered the same way. Null when that value is null.

derived_quarterly_value.description: The three-month figure derived from a year-to-date filing. A Q2/Q3 10-Q states YTD, so THIS and `numeric_value` are different numbers for the same fact — a verifier comparing against whichever one it happened to read passes wrong numbers half the time. Null when no derivation applies.

display.description: `numeric_value` ALREADY RENDERED — "$391.04B", "$6.11". QUOTE THIS character-for-character rather than re-rounding `numeric_value` yourself: the rendering also needs a scale, and `unit` alone cannot tell a fraction (0.5965 → "59.65%") from a percent (0.5965 → "0.60%"). Null when `numeric_value` is null.

document_url.description: Direct link to the rendered primary document (not the index page). Null when the primary document is unknown.

entity_id.description: Zero-padded 10-digit SEC CIK of the filer. (The key is named entity_id — there is no `cik` field.)

filing_date.description: Filing date (YYYY-MM-DD). Null when the filing join found nothing.

form_type.description: Filing form type — 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, 20-F. Null when the filing join found nothing.

inline_viewer_url.description: SEC Inline-XBRL viewer opened on the rendered primary document — the strongest one-click verification link. Null when the filing is not Inline-XBRL or the primary document is unknown.

numeric_value.description: The raw reported value. Null when the fact carries no numeric value.

period_end.description: End of the reporting window (YYYY-MM-DD), or the instant date for balance-sheet facts.

period_span_days.description: Length of the reporting window in days. Null when not derivable.

period_start.description: Start of the reporting window (YYYY-MM-DD). Null for instant (balance-sheet) facts.

period_type.description: Coarse duration class: instant | quarterly | half_year | nine_month | annual | duration. A single 10-K tags BOTH a 12-month figure and a 3-month Q4 stub at the same period_end, so this is what stops a stub being quoted as the annual number.

source_url.description: SEC filing-index URL. Null when the filing join found nothing.

standard_concept.description: Valuein's standardized concept name (TotalRevenue, NetIncome, …); null when the raw tag is unmapped.

ticker.description: Uppercase ticker the lookup resolved through.

unit.description: Unit of the value, e.g. USD, USD/share, shares.

lineage.description: Every lineage that resolved, keyed by fact_id — the filing behind each figure, so you can cite it without a second call. A fact that did NOT resolve is absent; its figure's verdict already says why.

differs.description: Figures the filing contradicts. Every one of these is a defect in the report.

matches.description: Figures whose quote is exactly what the filing says. The only affirmative count.

not_checkable.description: Figures that HAD a fact but could not be compared. ⚠️ Never report this as verified — it is expected to be large.

untraced.description: Figures that never had a fact to compare against. Counted apart from `not_checkable` so neither number misleads.

version.description: The report version verified. Null when unrecorded — a version we could not read is not version zero.

title: Verify Report Figures
